# 2003B Question 16 {.unnumbered}

::: {.exam-question}
## Question {.question-label}

[**Outline**]{.task-verb} the mechanism of secretion of hydrochloric acid by the stomach. [**Briefly describe**]{.task-verb} how secretion of hydrochloric acid by the stomach is controlled.
:::

:::: {#answer-structure}

## Suggested Structure

[**Outline**]{.task-verb} **Parietal Cell Secretion** using an ion-transport diagram, then [**briefly describe**]{.task-verb} **Receptor and Neural Control** and **Cephalic, Gastric and Intestinal Influences**.

::::

## Examiner Comments

::: {.examiner-comments}
**61%** of candidates passed this question.

The answers to the second part on control were often better than the first part on mechanism. Some candidates only answered the second part.

There were several important points that were often best dealt with by appropriate diagrams.

- The central role of the hydrogen/potassium ATPase.
- Receptors for gastrin, acetylcholine, and histamine.
- The role of the vagus.
- Multiple stimuli both enhancing and inhibiting acid secretion that many divided into cephalic, gastric, and intestinal factors.

Other issues included detailed descriptions of hydrogen ion formation using carbonic anhydrase and associated ion movements in and out of the parietal cells. Points attracting higher marks included a clear understanding that the stomach fluid is extremely acidic and that the parietal cells must actively secrete hydrogen ions against a considerable concentration gradient. Very few mentioned the role of canaliculi in inserting proton pumps into the cellular membrane when the parietal cells are stimulated.
:::
